newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mir repairs to be done by next crew.
newsitem.headline: Mir repairs to be done by next crew.

text.p: Risky repairs on the damaged Mir space station will be carried out by a relief crew which is due to blast off from Earth on August 5, a Russian space official said on Monday.

Deputy mission director Igor Goncharov told reporters the repairs would be done by Russian cosmonauts Anatoly Solovyov and Pavel Vinogradov after two of the current crew, Vasily Tsibliyev and Alexander Lazutkin, leave Mir on August 14.
"It was decided to hand over the repairs to the next crew. The repairs will be undertaken after the present crew leaves on August 14," Goncharov said at Korolyov Mission Control outside Moscow.

The decision was taken at a meeting of Russian space officials who also opted to exclude Frenchman Leopold Eyharts from the relief mission and said British-born NASA physicist Michael Foale would stay on Mir until mid-September.
Mir has been limping through space since a cargo craft hit it during a training docking on June 25, holing a module attached to Mir and damaging the power supply.

Lazutkin and Tsibliyev had hoped to repair the power supply, a risky operation involving them entering the airless module in spacesuits. But Tsibliyev developed an irregular heartbeat, one of a series of problems that has plagued the mission.
